title: EVERGREEN — Public Blueprint Library World

funnel.page0:
I want you to take one world in the Morverse, and that planet is going to be owned by the people who manage this library. And the library, it's actually going to be a public library. And I want you to make it luxurious and beautiful, and, like, just really plan out architecturally, make it elegant. Just make it a place that people want to be to learn and just, like, grow and just get information. Mor OS is a public open-source service. So, like, I want to be providing people as much as possible. So I need, like, normal social things that people show up to places to experience. But it's like this is going to be fucking crazy. Like, crazy levels of detail. But I need you to plan it, plan it end to end. End to end. And plan some expansions. Plan some expansions. But plan it end to end. To the damn wire blueprint. Super fucking blueprint. Ultra mega blueprint. Holy fuck, this blueprint's going to be blueprinting. And then build. Build it end to end.

Using the funnel. All using the funnel. This is all using the funnel, by the way. Don't forget that.
funnel.route: Page 0 → references → distill → decisions → replay → verdict
funnel.distilled_spec: Create EVERGREEN, a public Morverse library planet stewarded by its maintainers. The first release is a luxurious traversable civic library campus that makes blueprints, learning, making, social life, archival memory and compounding evergreen knowledge spatially legible. It must be genuinely usable as a 3D place, honest about network dependencies, connected to Pulse, and designed for planetary expansion.

locked_decisions.reason: Matches the user's evergreen compounding metaphor and remains editable later.
Managers hold world authority while a public-use covenant protects open access.
Supports luxury without turning into noisy sci-fi spectacle.

locked_decisions.value: Axial civic campus centered on Grand Rotunda
Program spaces first; real presence later through relay
Reserved districts → regional branches → planetary transit → interworld exchange

public_covenant: Public browsing is the default for canonical library holdings.
Forking and remix are first-class where source licenses permit.
Stewards may curate, preserve and moderate the public civic space but cannot silently erase historical versions.
Private working drafts remain private until their owner publishes them.
Canonical status means maintained and evidenced, not politically or aesthetically unquestionable.
non_goals: No invented legal land title mechanism in v1.
No paywall around the public canonical library.

principles: shade, water and trees as architecture
every major room has a reason to linger

materials.name: warm bronze
materials.use: doors, rails, trims, signage, knowledge plinths

materials.name: black water
materials.use: shallow reflecting pools and wayfinding axes

lighting.day: soft high daylight, warm sun, shaded arcades
lighting.night: dark-sky campus, path lights and observatory emphasis

scale_rules: Seating appears at least every 35 m of public path.
No endless empty monumental space without a human-scale edge.

world.climate: temperate evergreen highland around first library campus

zones.name: Arrival Terrace
zones.purpose: Give every visitor an immediate civic orientation before the library unfolds.
zones.architecture: Broad limestone stair, shallow water rills, bronze wayfinding monolith, framed axial view to the Rotunda.

zones.name: Forum of Questions
zones.purpose: A public square for questions, announcements, temporary exhibits and chance encounters.
zones.architecture: Oval stone forum around a black-water reflecting pool; low seat walls; colonnaded edges.

zones.name: Grand Rotunda
zones.purpose: Orient the whole knowledge world around one calm, memorable central room.
zones.architecture: Circular limestone drum, bronze ring, tall paired columns, glazed oculus and shallow copper-toned dome.

zones.name: Blueprint Stacks
zones.purpose: Browse systems as inspectable, forkable, buildable public blueprints.
zones.architecture: Long east gallery with repeated bays, oak tables, glass folio cases and a shaded arcade.

zones.name: Public Reading Hall
zones.purpose: Give people a beautiful place to stay for hours and actually learn.
zones.architecture: Long west hall with clerestory glazing, timber ceiling rhythm, warm reading lamps and garden views.

zones.name: Evergreen Grove
zones.purpose: Make reusable knowledge spatial and visible: plant once, keep yielding public value.
zones.architecture: Terraced garden of tall evergreen trees surrounding circular knowledge plinths and water channels.

zones.name: Makers Hall
zones.purpose: Turn public knowledge into working things and return the evidence to the library.
zones.architecture: Bronze-and-glass workshop hall with large doors, flexible bays, overhead service gantry and outdoor build court.

zones.name: Civic Amphitheater
zones.purpose: Give lectures, debates, performances and demonstrations a permanent civic stage.
zones.architecture: Sunken stone bowl in the landscape with a minimal timber stage and tree windbreak.

zones.name: Observatory of Unfinished Things
zones.purpose: Hold unresolved questions and frontier knowledge without pretending they are settled.
zones.architecture: Elevated circular observatory on a planted mound, dark metal dome, panoramic gallery and open roof deck.

zones.name: Social Commons
zones.purpose: Make ordinary hanging out a first-class library function instead of an afterthought.
zones.architecture: Courtyard café, communal tables, sheltered loggia, fireplace room and garden edge seating.

zones.name: Archive Vault
zones.purpose: Preserve canonical versions, provenance, failures and historical context.
zones.architecture: Quiet windowless stone volume partly embedded in grade; bronze portal; controlled inner gallery.

zones.name: Branch Gates
zones.purpose: Reserve the main axis for future districts and planetary branch libraries.
zones.architecture: Twin monumental gate frames terminating the current campus and pointing toward future planetary transit.

world.wayfinding: Major destinations are visible from the Forum or Rotunda; integrated map is optional rather than required to understand the campus.

physical_metaphors.failure: preserved case note in Archive, never erased

criteria: reused across multiple projects or domains
evergreen_promotion.result: Promoted into Evergreen Grove as a long-lived public reference; descendants and where-used links accumulate around it.

social_program.rule: Social life must be normal enough that people would visit even without a task.

recurring_formats.name: Open Build Night
recurring_formats.value: Build in public; working results return as evidence.

recurring_formats.name: Public Lecture
recurring_formats.value: Experts teach; recordings/transcripts become references when available.

recurring_formats.name: Salon of Unfinished Things
recurring_formats.value: Discuss unresolved questions without forcing premature consensus.

recurring_formats.name: Blueprint Crit
recurring_formats.value: Walk a system together and improve its requirements.

recurring_formats.name: Steward Open House
recurring_formats.value: Show maintenance decisions, planned changes and unresolved civic issues.

recurring_formats.name: Night Observatory
recurring_formats.value: Science/frontier talks and quiet sky viewing.

recurring_formats.name: World Festival
recurring_formats.value: Exhibitions, performances, demonstrations and branch exchange.

social_program.online_dependency: Real attendance, chat, invitations, calendar synchronization and avatar presence require the future live relay/account service. v1 builds spaces and program architecture only.

ui.human_request: Global MOOR request bar may appear as shared OS chrome; it is not the Funnel itself.
ui.agent_access: Agents call MOOR.request rather than typing into human UI.
ui.principle: World first; UI appears when useful and gets out of the view.

persistence: local last location and lighting preference only
library/reference truth remains outside scene UI

expansions.name: The Conservatory Belt
expansions.scope: Botanical library, material garden, seed archive, climate classrooms and outdoor studios encircling the first campus.

expansions.name: The College of Making
expansions.scope: Residencies, guild workshops, fabrication yards, long-form courses and public apprenticeship housing.

expansions.name: Regional Branches
expansions.scope: Distinct branch libraries in mountain, coast, forest and night-desert regions, each specializing in different knowledge domains.

expansions.name: Planetary Transit Ring
expansions.scope: Rail/portal network connecting branches, research preserves, cultural districts and the capital library.

expansions.name: Open Symposium Planet
expansions.scope: Planet-scale seasons of lectures, exhibitions, open-source summits and public build festivals.

expansions.name: Interworld Exchange
expansions.scope: Branch gates to other Morverse worlds; visiting exhibits, blueprint exchange and roaming public programs.

accessibility: Travel shortcuts for visitors who cannot/want not to walk the full campus.
Information never exists only as spatial placement; inspector/map provide equivalent structured access.
Major routes designed as level/ramped paths in the blueprint.
security_privacy: Public library holdings do not imply public personal drafts.
World UI never exposes secrets/API keys.
Moderation/presence must be server-authoritative when added.
Client-side ownership display is informational until an authoritative world service exists.
